preamble: Replacement of the voiced labiodental fricative [v] by the palatal glide [j], combining a large change of place with loss of friction. The clearest case is Southern (Saigon) Vietnamese, where /v/ is pronounced [j] in common speech and merges with d and gi, so that vợ 'wife' is [jə˨˧] beside Hanoi [və]. Careful speech and reading pronunciation increasingly restore [v].

examples.note: Southern merger of v with d and gi as [j] in everyday speech; in loanwords such as va li 'suitcase' the dialect uses [v], [ʋ] or [w] instead.
